name: Alexander the coppersmith
charge: Doing Paul much evil; greatly withstanding his words
summary: In the uproar at Ephesus the Jews put Alexander forward out of the multitude to make a defence, and the crowd shouted him down for about two hours once they knew what he was (Acts 19:33-34). Paul later names Alexander with Hymenaeus among those who made shipwreck of the faith and were delivered to Satan that they might learn not to blaspheme (1 Timothy 1:19-20), and at the end writes that Alexander the coppersmith did him much evil and greatly withstood their words, and that the Lord would reward him according to his works (2 Timothy 4:14-15).
offenseFull: Alexander first appears in the city of the silversmiths. Demetrius had stirred the craftsmen over the shrines of Diana, the town was in confusion, and the Jews pushed Alexander forward; he beckoned with his hand and would have made his defence to the people, but when they knew he was a Jew they cried up their goddess for about two hours instead (Acts 19:24-27; Acts 19:33-34). The teaching reads him plainly: he was a coppersmith in the city where the trade was making idols, which is where Paul met him, and for a moment he stood between Paul’s companions and a mob. One teacher takes it further and says that once the crowd turned he went along with the foolishness.

Whatever he was then, he did not stay. Paul names him with Hymenaeus among those who put away faith and a good conscience and made shipwreck concerning the faith, and delivered them to Satan that they might learn not to blaspheme (1 Timothy 1:19-20), after charging Timothy with the same commission that he might war a good warfare (1 Timothy 1:18). In the last chapter Paul ever wrote he returns to him: Alexander the coppersmith did me much evil, and Timothy is told to beware of him also, for he greatly withstood our words (2 Timothy 4:14-15). Put the weight where it belongs. Imagine being in the ministry and then turning against the ministry. That was this man, and Paul writes it in the same breath as the line that at his first answer no man stood with him and all men forsook him (2 Timothy 4:16).
judgmentFull: Paul did not lift a hand and did not ask anybody else to. He said, the Lord reward him according to his works (2 Timothy 4:14). That is the law he taught: avenge not yourselves, for vengeance belongs to God, who will repay (Romans 12:19), and mercy belongs to the Lord, for he renders to every man according to his work (Psalms 62:12). Paul had been the chief of persecutors himself and obtained mercy, so he was not looking to destroy this man. He was keeping order and leaving the account where accounts are settled.

What Paul does command is separation. Mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine which you have learned, and avoid them (Romans 16:17). Under Moses a man who drew the people after another doctrine was to be stoned and the hand of the witness first upon him (Deuteronomy 13:6-10); in Christ the body cuts him off and nothing more, and the words passed to Timothy are a warning to a young leader, not an execution. In the same passage where he asks the Lord to repay Alexander, Paul prays that the forsaking of the others be not laid to their charge, and records that notwithstanding, the Lord stood with him and strengthened him, so that the preaching might be fully known and he was delivered out of the mouth of the lion (2 Timothy 4:16-17). The case stands as cursed on the word Paul spoke over him. The carrying out of it is not in the book.

taught.title: Psalm 62: Let Your Expectation Be of God
Deuteronomy 13: Enticers to Other Gods Put Away

text.text: For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith, which made silver shrines for Diana, brought no small gain unto the craftsmen;
Whom he called together with the workmen of like occupation, and said, Sirs, ye know that by this craft we have our wealth.
Moreover ye see and hear, that not alone at Ephesus, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul hath persuaded and turned away much people, saying that they be no gods, which are made with hands:

So that not only this our craft is in danger to be set at nought; but also that the temple of the great goddess Diana should be despised, and her magnificence should be destroyed, whom all Asia and the world worshippeth.
And they drew Alexander out of the multitude, the Jews putting him forward. And Alexander beckoned with the hand, and would have made his defence unto the people.
But when they knew that he was a Jew, all with one voice about the space of two hours cried out, Great is Diana of the Ephesians.
This charge I commit unto thee, son Timothy, according to the prophecies which went before on thee, that thou by them mightest war a good warfare;
Holding faith, and a good conscience; which some having put away concerning faith have made shipwreck:
Of whom is Hymeneus and Alexander; whom I have delivered unto Satan, that they may learn not to blaspheme.
Alexander the coppersmith did me much evil: the Lord reward him according to his works:
Of whom be thou ware also; for he hath greatly withstood our words.
At my first answer no man stood with me, but all men forsook me: I pray God that it may not be laid to their charge.
Notwithstanding the Lord stood with me, and strengthened me; that by me the preaching might be fully known, and that all the Gentiles might hear: and I was delivered out of the mouth of the lion.
Dearly beloved, avenge not yourselves, but rather give place unto wrath: for it is written, Vengeance is mine; I will repay, saith the Lord.
Also unto thee, O Lord, belongeth mercy: for thou renderest to every man according to his work.
Now I beseech you, brethren, mark them which cause divisions and offences contrary to the doctrine which ye have learned; and avoid them.

If thy brother, the son of thy mother, or thy son, or thy daughter, or the wife of thy bosom, or thy friend, which is as thine own soul, entice thee secretly, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, which thou hast not known, thou, nor thy fathers;
Namely, of the gods of the people which are round about you, nigh unto thee, or far off from thee, from the one end of the earth even unto the other end of the earth;
Thou shalt not consent unto him, nor hearken unto him; neither shall thine eye pity him, neither shalt thou spare, neither shalt thou conceal him:
But thou shalt surely kill him; thine hand shall be first upon him to put him to death, and afterwards the hand of all the people.
And thou shalt stone him with stones, that he die; because he hath sought to thrust thee away from the Lord thy God, which brought thee out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage.
